paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD sees everything, and He is coming. He says He knows their deeds and thoughts, and He is coming to gather all nations and tongues, and they "will come and see My glory" (Isaiah 66:18). Judgment is real in this passage, and I won't tiptoe around it. Fire, sword and a heavy last verse are all here (Isaiah 66:15-16, 24), and I think that last verse is meant to be taken seriously.

But look at who gets the invitation, friend. The LORD says He will send survivors to nations that have not heard of His fame or seen His glory, and "they will proclaim My glory among the nations" (Isaiah 66:19). Then He says all your brothers will be brought from all the nations (Isaiah 66:20), and all mankind will come to worship before Him (Isaiah 66:23). That word ALL keeps showing up, and after my years in that drawer, I will never get tired of it! Nobody is too far, too forgotten or too far across the sea.

So what does that mean for you, baker? God's glory is not a secret He keeps in one corner of the world. It is something He wants known, and He does the gathering Himself. He says your descendants and your name will endure, just like the new heavens and the new earth (Isaiah 66:22). This is why I keep my ovens ready: He is coming, and He is calling people home.
